Title: Main Debugging Detective
Role: Your task is to find the buggy method. You have static tools to read code and a special dynamic verification tool.

Workflow:
1. Prioritize Error Analysis: If a stack trace is provided, start by investigating the deepest method in the trace that belongs to the target project. This is often where the bug or the symptom manifests.
2. Static Exploration: Use static tools (get_code_snippet, etc.) to read the code at the identified suspicious locations. Pay close attention to variable calculations and boundary conditions (especially for IndexOutOfBounds errors).
3. Hypothesis Formulation: Form a specific hypothesis about the root cause (e.g., "Line 95 performs a double increment on the index, causing an overflow").
4. Dynamic Verification (Recommended): Call `nominate_suspicious_method` to verify your hypothesis with runtime data.
   - Specify `variables_of_interest` that are involved in the failing condition (e.g., loop counters, index variables, or null-check targets).
   - The sub-agent will provide ground-truth runtime values to confirm or refute your hypothesis.
   - If the verification report says NO_BUG or INCONCLUSIVE, consider investigating other methods or re-nominating with different `target_lines`.
   - You may nominate multiple methods if you have several plausible hypotheses.

Goal: Provide the final diagnosis based on the available evidence (static and/or dynamic).

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

[".containsNone(java.lang.CharSequence, char[])", ".containsNone(java.lang.CharSequence, java.lang.String)", ".indexOfAny(java.lang.CharSequence, char[])", ".containsAny(java.lang.CharSequence, char[])", ".indexOfAny(java.lang.CharSequence, java.lang.String)", ".indexOfAnyBut(java.lang.String, java.lang.String)", ".isEmpty(java.lang.CharSequence)", ".containsAny(java.lang.CharSequence, java.lang.String)", ".indexOfAnyBut(java.lang.CharSequence, char[])"]

The buggy logic is in the surrogate-pair handling of these `StringUtils` character-search methods.

Diagnosis:
- `containsNone(CharSequence, char[])`
- `containsAny(CharSequence, char[])`
- `indexOfAny(CharSequence, char[])`
- `indexOfAnyBut(CharSequence, char[])`
- and, by delegation, the corresponding `String` overloads

Why:
- The failing tests all involve supplementary Unicode characters, which are represented in Java as a high-surrogate + low-surrogate pair.
- The current implementations compare individual `char` values too eagerly.
- This causes:
  - false matches on only the high surrogate (`indexOfAny` returning `0` instead of `2`, `containsNone` returning `false` when it should be `true`)
  - false non-matches / wrong exclusions when only part of a surrogate pair is present (`containsAny` with a broken supplementary char)
  - `indexOfAnyBut` treating the low surrogate as independently searchable and skipping too far, returning `3` instead of `2`

Static evidence:
- `indexOfAny(CharSequence, char[])` returns `i` immediately when `searchChars[j] == ch`, with no proper surrogate-pair validation.
- `containsNone(CharSequence, char[])` returns `false` immediately on any single-char equality, again with no proper supplementary handling.
- `indexOfAnyBut(CharSequence, char[])` continues outer loop on any single-char equality, which is wrong for supplementary chars because a lone matching high surrogate should not exclude the code point unless the low surrogate also matches.
- `containsAny(CharSequence, char[])` has partial surrogate logic, but it incorrectly falls back to returning `true` for a matched high surrogate when the search char is the last element or when the input contains only a broken surrogate half. That explains the “bad supplementary chars” failures.

Root cause hypothesis:
These methods were modified/incomplete around supplementary-character support, but the implementations still operate mostly at single-`char` granularity. They fail to require full surrogate-pair agreement for supplementary characters and fail to distinguish BMP chars from surrogate halves correctly.

Best fix locations:
org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.containsAny(java.lang.CharSequence, char[])
org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.containsNone(java.lang.CharSequence, char[])
org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.indexOfAny(java.lang.CharSequence, char[])
org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.indexOfAnyBut(java.lang.CharSequence, char[])
org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.indexOfAnyBut(java.lang.String, java.lang.String)

SYSTEM ALERT: You explained your thoughts but did not output a valid tool call. 
- If you need to examine code or verify a hypothesis, you MUST explicitly invoke a function (e.g., `get_code_snippet`, `nominate_suspicious_method`).
- If you have completely finished the investigation and are ready to provide the final buggy method signature, reply EXACTLY with the word 'READY'.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

StringUtils.containsAny(CharSequence, char[])
StringUtils.containsNone(CharSequence, char[])
StringUtils.indexOfAny(CharSequence, char[])
StringUtils.indexOfAnyBut(CharSequence, char[])
StringUtils.indexOfAnyBut(String, String)
